articles.title: Salford girl, 7, wins national Lowry art prize
articles.summary: Mia says she is "really happy" to have her artwork on display in the Lowry museum.
articles.body:
A seven-year-old girl has won a national competition for her artwork which was inspired by LS Lowry.

Mia, of Salford, was picked as the winner from 600 entries to the 2026 Copley Prize, an annual art competition run by the Lowry theatre and gallery.

Her artwork, titled A Man Going To Work, is now hanging in the Andrew Law Galleries, alongside the famous paintings by Lowry himself, and will remain on display for the next 12 months.

Mia said: "I feel so happy that my work will be in a real art gallery."

Every year primary school-aged children from across the UK are invited to submit artwork inspired by LS Lowry to Lowry's Copley Prize.

Mia's work was chosen as this year's overall winner by Alison and Noel Copley who are huge admirers of LS Lowry's work and long-standing supporters of the Lowry's programmes for children and young people.

They founded the art competition in 2013 as a way to encourage primary-aged children to develop their creativity and artistic ability.

Alison Copley said: "LS Lowry's work is evident as the inspiration behind Mia's superb artwork - a man going about his daily life, but with such character and detail that we see this ordinary person with a fresh perspective.

"Mia is a very talented artist and we hope she and the other wonderful entrants of this year's Copley Prize keep on making and creating art."

articles.title: It's sweet, it's green and it's fluffy. How a Swedish princess cake became an online obsession.
articles.summary: Meet the internet's latest obsession: the Swedish princess cake.
articles.body:
What's green, spongy, has a raspberry jam filling and hails from Sweden? A Swedish princess cake, of course! Beloved for its playful, pastel-green color and perfectly domed shape, the dainty confection — also known as prinsesstårta — has become a social media sensation after TikTokers learned that Trader Joe's just unveiled its own version.

"OK, breaking news — I just found out Trader Joe's is doing a princess cake, and I haven't even got it yet. I had no idea this was a thing… Somebody posted this, I thought it was AI," a TikToker named Samantha said in a recent video, which has garnered nearly 26,000 likes. "Umm, apparently it's real. The only complaint that I already have is why is it limited time? Because I feel like if it's good, I'm gonna cry when I can't get this."

What has the internet hooked on this cake? And why does it look so familiar? Here's what to know about the fairytale-like dessert drawing attention to Trader Joe's freezers.

Trader Joe's unveiled its "Swedish Princess Raspberry Cake" in late September. The 18-ounce dessert costs $7.99 and comes in a pretty pink box featuring an image of the cake on a white platter. The Trader Joe's princess cake, per the dessert's online description , is made "by experts in Sweden" and will be available in stores from now through the end of the year.

"It's a traditional domed confection that features two layers of airy sponge cake sandwiching a thin layer of tart-sweet raspberry jam and rich pastry cream," reads the dessert's description. "On top of this is a lusciously thick dome (we mean thick!) of whipped cream, with the entire Cake draped in stunning, pastel-green marzipan that's accented with thin white stripes. There's really nothing quite like this combination, either in look or in taste!"

News that Trader Joe's unveiled a freezer-friendly version of the cake spread fast. On TikTok, several happy customers have shared videos of themselves unboxing and trying the princess cake for the first time.

Rachel, a content creator who goes by @eatsbyrachel on TikTok, posted her taste test video on Wednesday. She said IKEA previously released its own princess cake, though "it was a complete miss" when she tried it. (One redditor claimed the IKEA version was " sickly sweet " for their palate.)

"It defrosted pretty nicely, and we have clean layers of cream, cake and raspberry jam," Rachel said. "The cream is perfectly light and fluffy, and the raspberry jam kind of cuts through it. And the marzipan layer on the outside isn't too thick, which I appreciate… and the cake itself is also really light and fluffy."

Lily Beez, another content creator, also shared her review of the Trader Joe's dessert on Wednesday.

"TJ's, I'm impressed," Beez said after taking her first bite. "The cream is definitely very fluffy and light. You can absolutely taste the raspberry. The marzipan isn't too thick and gloopy either. Overall, for $8, this is a great find. I feel like it would be really cute for somebody's birthday with just one singular candle in the middle."

Its connection to 'The Great British Bake Off'

If the viral cake looks familiar, that's because it is. Fans of The Great British Bake Off may remember seeing the Swedish princess cake in a Season 5 episode titled "European Cakes." During the episode's technical challenge, judge Mary Berry asks the six bakers to recreate her complicated, 24-step recipe for the showstopping green cake in less than three hours.

The Swedish princess cake also has royal ties. Jenny Åkerström, the author and home economics teacher credited with inventing the cake, taught Swedish princesses, Margaretha, Märtha and Astrid, the daughters of Prince Carl, Duke of Västergötland, in the early 20th century. A recipe for the cake appeared in a later edition of Åkerström's cookbook, Prinsessornas kokbok or Cookbook of the Princesses . The now-viral dessert was originally known as "green cake" or grön tårta, but was renamed "princess cake" or prinsesstårta because the princesses were said to have loved it.

So why is a frozen Trader Joe's dessert charming the internet? And is the hype even warranted? Beyond its novelty as a limited-edition sweet treat, the TJ's Swedish princess cake is a whimsical confection that seems to bring people joy. On Reddit , users have shared their excitement over the traditional Swedish dessert. Many associate it with beloved family members and nostalgic childhood memories.

"Oh my god. This is literally my favorite dessert in the entire world," a redditor commented . "It evokes in me a Proustian sense memory of eating it as a child any time I somehow manage to get it, but those occasions are few and far between."

Another added , "There was a Swedish bakery, Crown bakery in Worcester, MA for over fifty years. They made Princess cakes, Swedish coffee cake rings. The rolled out fondant, covering the whole cake. Many times visiting family, they would either have a Swedish coffee cake or Princess cake. Fond memories of delicious desserts."

For others, its appeal is far simpler. As one Reddit user put it , "Call me a basic b, but you put princess in the name and my inner child wants it (also I love custard)."

articles.title: Justiça solta pais suspeitos de maus-tratos a filhos em Americana | G1
articles.standfirst: Justiça apontou que não há "demonstração de situação flagrancial" para manter prisões. Filhos foram encaminhados a familiares e estão sendo acompanhados pelo Conselho Tutelar.
articles.summary: Justiça apontou que não há "demonstração de situação flagrancial" para manter prisões. Filhos foram encaminhados a familiares e estão sendo acompanhados pelo Conselho Tutelar.
articles.body:
A Justiça decidiu nesta sexta-feira (25), em audiência de custódia, soltar um casal que foi preso na manhã desta quinta (24) por suspeita de maus-tratos aos filhos, de 10 e 14 anos , no bairro Monte Verde, em Americana (SP). Na decisão, o juiz apontou ilegalidade nas prisões, já que não há "demonstração de situação flagrancial".

Mesmo com as solturas, os menores de idade foram encaminhados a familiares e estão sendo acompanhados pelo Conselho Tutelar. Eles só poderão voltar a morar com o casal se tiver determinação judicial .

O Tribunal de Justiça do Estado de São Paulo (TJ-SP) explicou que o relaxamento de prisão em flagrante é a ordem do juiz para soltar imediatamente uma pessoa que foi presa de forma errônea ou ilegal.

Ainda segundo o TJ, o caso tramita sob sigilo.

Casal é preso por maus-tratos após filhos serem achados em casa cheia de lixo em Americana — Foto: Divulgação

De acordo com o boletim de ocorrência, a mulher tem 41 anos e o homem, 33. Na casa da família, os agentes encontraram grande acúmulo de lixo e objetos, restos de comida estragada, cheiro forte e sinais de insetos pela casa. As condições do local prejudicavam a saúde e o bem-estar.

O caso foi descoberto após a escola da adolescente informar ao Conselho Tutelar que ela estaria se automutilando. Questionado, o pai afirmou à polícia que a limpeza da casa era responsabilidade da filha e a culpou pela sujeira.

O casal ainda teria admitido que sabia das más condições da casa, mas não tomou providências para garantir um ambiente limpo e seguro para os filhos. O pai também teria dito que não sabia da automutilação da adolescente.

Diante do cenário, o Conselho Tutelar acionou a Vigilância Sanitária. O homem e a mulher foram levados à Delegacia de Defesa da Mulher (DDM) de Americana.

O caso foi registrado no 4º Distrito Policial da cidade como maus-tratos, violência psicológica e submissão de criança ou adolescente a vexame .

articles.title: São José registra forte queda nos índices de criminalidade | G1
articles.standfirst: Dados da SSP mostram redução em roubos, furtos de veículos, homicídios e outros crimes na comparação entre janeiro e julho de 2016 e 2026.
articles.summary: Dados da SSP mostram redução em roubos, furtos de veículos, homicídios e outros crimes na comparação entre janeiro e julho de 2016 e 2026.
articles.body:
São José dos Campos segue avançando na segurança pública. Os indicadores criminais referentes aos primeiros sete meses de 2026 confirmam a redução dos principais crimes registrados no município, na comparação com o mesmo período de 2016.

O destaque fica para os roubos de veículos, que apresentaram redução de 97,9%: foram 493 ocorrências entre janeiro e julho de 2016, contra 25 no mesmo período deste ano.

A queda também aparece em outros importantes indicadores. Os roubos em geral tiveram redução de 85,5%, passando de 2.445 casos para 355. Já os furtos de veículos caíram 71,6%, de 1.308 para 371 ocorrências.

Os homicídios também apresentaram redução significativa, de 56,1%, passando de 41 registros nos primeiros sete meses de 2016 para 18 em 2026. Nos furtos em geral, a redução foi de 22,8%, com 2.795 ocorrências neste ano, ante 3.622 em 2016.

articles.summary: Decisão foi publicada na quinta-feira (24) e não impôs nenhuma condição às empresas para que negócio fosse fechado. Concorrentes ainda podem recorrer da decisão.
articles.body:
Supermercados BH, EPA e Mineirão assinam acordo para unir operações em MG e outros três estados — Foto: Reprodução/Redes sociais

O Conselho Administrativo de Defesa Econômica (Cade), órgão do governo federal que fiscaliza a concorrência entre empresas, aprovou sem restrições a compra de 114 lojas do Grupo DMA, dono das marcas Epa e Mineirão, pelo Supermercados BH .

As unidades ficam em 19 cidades mineiras, e 75 delas estão em Belo Horizonte (veja a lista completa ao final da reportagem) . A negociação começou em abril e previa 120 lojas, mas seis foram retiradas depois que o órgão apontou risco de concentração de mercado.

Entenda, abaixo, os principais pontos da negociação:

São 114 unidades das bandeiras Epa Plus, Epa Premium e Mineirão , sendo 103 supermercados e 11 atacarejos.

As lojas estão espalhadas por cidades da Região Metropolitana, Campo das Vertentes, Zona da Mata, Central Mineira, Vale do Rio Doce e Sul de Minas (veja a lista completa ao final da reportagem) .

Belo Horizonte concentra 75 lojas, seguida por Contagem, com 10, e Ribeirão das Neves, com 5.

As lojas do Epa vão virar Supermercados BH?

As empresas ainda não informaram. Nos documentos entregues ao governo, elas afirmam que a compra permite "a expansão da bandeira do Supermercados BH" em cidades onde a rede não está presente ou tem pouca presença.

O contrato de compra e venda, que traria a resposta, está sob sigilo a pedido das companhias . O que está sendo comprado é o ponto comercial e as instalações; ou seja, as marcas Epa e Mineirão continuam pertencendo ao Grupo DMA.

Não. A aprovação foi dada pela Superintendência-Geral do Cade, primeira instância do órgão. A partir da publicação no Diário Oficial, corre um prazo de 15 dias em que a decisão pode ser contestada , seja por empresas que já estavam formalmente cadastradas no processo, seja por iniciativa dos próprios conselheiros do órgão.

Se isso acontecer, a compra fica parada até um novo julgamento pelo Tribunal do órgão. Se o prazo terminar sem contestação, as empresas ficam liberadas para concluir a transação.

Em nota, o Supermercados BH disse que vai "observar os prazos e demais trâmites legais previstos, até que todas as etapas sejam formalmente concluídas".

O g1 procurou o Epa, mas não obteve resposta até a última atualização desta reportagem.

Em 31 de agosto, o órgão classificou o caso como complexo. Segundo a análise técnica, faltavam provas de que houvesse concorrência suficiente nas regiões em torno de algumas unidades. Em um dos casos, a participação somada das duas redes no mercado local ficava entre 80% e 90%.

Antes, ainda em agosto, a análise técnica do órgão apontou risco de concentração em seis regiões onde havia, ao todo, 12 lojas do Grupo DMA, o que totalizariam 108 unidades compradas pelos Supermercados BH.

A decisão final, porém, retirou do negócio apenas seis unidades e confirmou a compra de 114 lojas.

Veneza, em Ribeirão das Neves; Vila Joana D'Arc, em Lagoa Santa; Venda Nova, em Belo Horizonte; Siderurgia, em Ouro Branco; Cinira de Freitas, em Sarzedo; e Distrito Industrial, em Itajubá.

Essas unidades seguem sendo do Grupo DMA, que seguirá com 17 lojas próprias em Minas Gerais.

Como o governo concluiu que não haveria prejuízo ao consumidor?

A análise foi feita região por região. Em Belo Horizonte, foram examinadas 67 áreas diferentes, uma para cada loja.

O critério foi medir quanto tempo o consumidor levaria de carro para chegar a um concorrente, em um sábado às 11h.

Em cidades menores, considerou-se o limite do próprio município. O órgão concluiu que não é provável que o Supermercados BH consiga abusar de sua posição, citando a presença de redes como Carrefour, Assaí, Mart Minas, Verdemar, Villefort, Multiformato e Economart, a abertura de 92 lojas novas na capital entre 2021 e 2025 e o crescimento do faturamento do setor.

Sim. Várias redes concorrentes não responderam ao questionário enviado pelo governo, e por isso a fatia de mercado calculada para o Supermercados BH pode estar maior do que é na realidade.

Em algumas cidades, mesmo com a aprovação, a concentração ficou alta: em Ponte Nova, por exemplo, a participação somada das duas redes ficou entre 60% e 70% do mercado local.

Que tamanho o Supermercados BH passa a ter?

A rede já é a maior de Minas Gerais e a quarta do Brasil, com faturamento de R$ 25,7 bilhões em 2025 , segundo a Associação Brasileira de Supermercados (Abras).

Com a compra, a receita pode chegar a cerca de R$ 34,6 bilhões , de acordo com projeções da Federação das Câmaras de Dirigentes Lojistas de Minas Gerais, com base nos números da Abras.

Esta é a segunda operação entre as duas empresas no ano: a primeira, com 40 lojas em Minas, na Bahia e em Pernambuco, foi aprovada em maio .

articles.title: Nova lei proíbe venda de animais em locais como Mercado Central em BH | G1
articles.standfirst: Norma publicada nesta sexta-feira (25) proíbe venda de animais vivos em vias públicas, espaços abertos e locais de grande fluxo turístico ou tradicionalmente destinados à exposição cultural e gastronômica.
articles.summary: Norma publicada nesta sexta (25) proíbe venda de animais vivos em locais de grande fluxo turístico ou tradicionalmente destinados à exposição cultural e gastronômica.
articles.body:
Animais à venda no Mercado Central forma apreendidos — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

O prefeito de Belo Horizonte, Álvaro Damião (União Brasil), sancionou a lei que proíbe a venda de animais vivos em vias públicas, espaços abertos e locais de grande fluxo turístico ou tradicionalmente destinados à exposição cultural e gastronômica, como o Mercado Central. O texto foi publicado no Diário Oficial do Município nesta sexta-feira (25).

A norma estabelece que a reprodução e o comércio de animais domésticos só poderão ser realizados em canis, gatis e criadouros cadastrados e licenciados pelo poder público municipal.

Esses estabelecimentos deverão ter responsável técnico inscrito no conselho profissional competente e observar normas sanitárias, ambientais e de bem-estar animal.

Além disso, locais que trabalham com a venda ou a doação de animais deverão identificá-los com microchip ou outro sistema reconhecido pela autoridade sanitária, além de entregar os bichos vacinados e desverminados. Eles também deverão repassar aos adquirentes material informativo sobre adoção e guarda responsável.

A lei entra em vigor 120 dias após a publicação. O g1 questionou o Mercado Central sobre o assunto, mas não obteve retorno até a última atualização desta reportagem.

A lei, proveniente de um projeto do vereador Osvaldo Lopes (Podemos), aprovado em 2º turno pela Câmara Municipal no dia 10 de agosto , atende a uma demanda antiga de grupos de defesa da causa animal, que protestam há anos contra a comercialização de bichos no Mercado Central.

Em 2016, o Ministério Público de Minas Gerais (MPMG) entrou com uma ação civil pública contra a comercialização de bichos no local e conseguiu uma liminar , que foi cassada posteriormente.

Em 2018, a Câmara Municipal chegou a aprovar um projeto de lei que tornava mais rígidas as regras para a venda de animais domésticos, mas a proposta foi vetada pelo então prefeito Alexandre Kalil.

articles.title: 'Mafia ruled UP, Yogi govt eliminated it': Amit Shah highlights political stability, policy implementation under BJP govt
articles.summary: NOIDA: Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Friday said the BJP government had eliminated the mafia from Uttar Pradesh, creating a conducive atmosphere for
articles.body: NOIDA: Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Friday said the BJP government had eliminated the mafia from Uttar Pradesh, creating a conducive atmosphere for investment in the state.Addressing the UP International Trade Show 2026, Shah recalled the situation in the state before the BJP came to power in 2017 and said the Yogi Adityanath government had taken steps to eliminate mafia elements across Uttar Pradesh."There was a time when the mafia ruled UP. In 2017, the BJP formed the government here, with Yogi Adityanath assuming the role of Chief Minister. The Yogi government has successfully eliminated the mafia across the state, and this has created a conducive atmosphere for investment..." Shah said.He also highlighted political stability under Prime Minister Narendra Modi and said policy continuity and implementation had helped transform India into a global manufacturing hub."Political stability has become a hallmark of our leader, PM Modi. By earning the public's trust over 3 consecutive terms as Prime Minister, he has not only formulated policies but also ensured their consistent implementation on the ground, he said.Shah added that "PM Modi has also demonstrated great dynamism in refining existing policies and formulating new ones based on experience, thereby transforming India into an attractive global manufacturing hub."The Union home minister recalled that in 2013, the Uttar Pradesh government had organised a conference to attract industrial investment to the state, but the event had to be held in Delhi due to the law-and-order situation in Lucknow."In 2013, UP govt organised a conference to attract industrial investment to the state... At that time, it had to be held in Delhi. When the media raised questions about this, UP officials frankly admitted that the law-and-order situation in Lucknow was such that no investor was willing to come there. That is why they had to move the event to Delhi," Shah said.He contrasted the situation with the present and credited the change to the "double-engine" government."But look at the situation today: That very same Uttar Pradesh has become free from fear, a hub for investment, and an engine of national growth. This transformation is the magic of the 'double-engine' government," he said.Shah said the transformation had enabled Uttar Pradesh to set an ambitious target of becoming a USD 1 trillion economy."It is precisely because of this transformation that Uttar Pradesh can now set the ambitious goal of becoming a 1-trillion-dollar economy," he said.Shah contrasted the present situation in Uttar Pradesh with the period when the Samajwadi Party and Bahujan Samaj Party governed the state, and highlighted the emergence of new industrial and manufacturing sectors."There was a time when the SP and BSP ruled here. A 'crime industry' was thriving... Look at the situation today, 10 years later. In place of the illegal pistol industry, a defence corridor has been established; vehicle manufacturing has replaced vehicle theft; and a medical device park is coming up where the chain-snatching 'industry' once existed. This is a massive transformation," Shah said.He said Uttar Pradesh, which earlier lacked confidence to host an investment summit in Lucknow, had now emerged as a major destination for investors."The very UP that once lacked the confidence to host an investment summit in Lucknow has now become a major hub for attracting investment... After the Yogi government took office, the BJP administration completely eradicated the hooliganism that prevailed during the SP-BSP era..." he said.Shah also highlighted the impact of the One District One Product (ODOP) initiative on employment and local manufacturing in the state."There was a time when people from here used to travel to states across the country in search of employment. Today, however, the youth of UP are finding jobs right here in their own state because of this (One District One Product) initiative," he said.He said the ODOP website had been launched to further promote the state's products and manufacturers."I have just launched the ODOP website... This trade show will greatly facilitate business and production for UP's manufacturers and help showcase the state's identity to the world," Shah said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: You may not be cleaning your makeup brushes enough — here’s what experts recommend
articles.summary: Dirty makeup brushes can cause breakouts and irritation. Experts share how often to clean your brushes and sponges, plus the best cleaners to get the job done.
articles.body: With all the content available online these days, it can be hard to figure out what’s real and what’s hype. While we don’t always have the answers, we have a direct line to people who do — which is why we present to you our series The Internet Made Me Ask, where we have experts break down the truth about some of the buzziest trends on our timelines, like how often you should wash jeans. Makeup brushes do a lot of work — namely sweeping foundation, blush, powder and other cosmetics onto your face day after day — yet many people rarely think about cleaning them. It’s an easy chore to put off, especially since freshly washed brushes can take up to 24 hours to dry. The only problem with that is that skipping regular cleanings can affect both how your makeup looks and the health of your skin. “[Not cleaning makeup brushes] can lead to makeup buildup on the brush hairs, which can negatively affect the softness of the bristles over time and lead to a patchy or streaky application,” says Eric Vosburg, a New York City-based makeup artist. “And due to the high moisture content from liquid and cream products, bacteria can easily form and grow, which can cause the contaminated tools to spread bacteria around the skin, leading to acne.” So, how often should you actually be washing them? I posed that very question to Vosburg and other professional makeup artists and got tips on the best way to actually wash them and recommendations on tools that can help you get the job done. How often should you clean your makeup brushes? How often you should wash your makeup brushes depends on how frequently you use them and what you use them for. As a general rule, Vosburg recommends cleaning them once a week to reduce product buildup and keep bristles in good condition. Brushes used with liquid or cream formulas, like foundation and concealer, tend to collect residue and moisture faster than those used with powders, so they need attention more frequently — you may be able to stretch wash time on powder brushes to every two weeks. Certain situations also call for extra cleanings. If you’ve recently been sick, wash your brushes once you’ve recovered to avoid transferring germs back onto your skin or into your makeup products. And if you’re dealing with acne or breakouts, more frequent cleaning can help limit the spread of bacteria and fungus and prevent reinfection, says Zac Hart, a New York City-based hair and makeup artist. Between deep cleanings, a quick-dry brush cleaner can be a convenient option, since it removes residue and sanitizes bristles without the long drying time. However, relying on these sprays too often can damage brushes over time and they can leave behind a residue of their own, says Hart. In other words, use them sparingly and only when you absolutely need a quick clean until you’re able to do a thorough one. The best products to clean makeup brushes To help you get your makeup brushes as clean as possible, I asked Vosburg and Hart what types of products can be helpful. I then sourced highly-rated options within the categories they recommended. All of the products below have at least a four-star average rating from more than a thousand shoppers. Vosburg says a simple, mild bar soap is a great cleanser for makeup brushes because you can simply swirl your brush over it to work up a lather. This fragrance-free option from Cetaphil is designed for dry, sensitive skin, so it cleans gently and can help lift away makeup residue while being easy on both synthetic and natural bristles. I’ve been using this cleanser on my makeup brushes for years. I like that it’s gentle enough for my most expensive brushes while still getting them super clean. The sulfate-free liquid formula lathers easily and cuts through stubborn foundation and concealer buildup. It works just as well on sponges, and its light lavender scent leaves tools smelling fresh. I set this silicone bowl up next to my sink whenever I clean my brushes. The textured ridges inside help loosen makeup buildup as I swirl each brush through soap and water, making the process quicker and less messy. I also like that the bowl is collapsible, so it folds flat and tucks away easily for storage. This rinse-free formula is good if you are in a pinch and don’t have time to dry your brushes. It cleans natural and synthetic bristles, dissolving foundation, powder, and color buildup while deodorizing and hydrating them. It also dries quickly, so brushes are ready to use again in moments. This electric spinner takes almost all of the manual work out of cleaning makeup brushes. You attach a brush to the device using one of the included rubber collars, dip it into the bowl of soapy water and let it spin clean. Lifting it out of the water while spinning helps get rid of excess moisture, which can help speed up drying time. NBC Selected senior editor Shalwah Evans started using this makeup brush cleaner earlier this year and says it works faster than any other cleaner she’s ever used. “I have the tin from the travel kit and I just pour the solution into the tin, dip my brush halfway and then watch all the dirty liquid just pour off of the brush and into the sink. It’s gross and fascinating at the same time,” she says. “I love that I don’t have to do a bunch of scrubbing like I do with bar soaps and the residue comes off when I rinse it under the faucet. The gnarly smell is definitely the one drawback, but it’s nothing one pump of hand soap can’t take away.” How do you clean makeup brushes? Before you start cleaning, it helps to know what your brushes are made of, since synthetic and natural bristles need slightly different care. Vosburg breaks down those two most common types of brushes below. Synthetic brushes: Many makeup brushes, especially foundation and lip brushes, are made with synthetic fibers. Because they’re typically used with liquid and cream products, they can hold onto oily buildup that’s tough to remove. A simple soap works well here, since it breaks down oils quickly and gets synthetic bristles clean without much effort.Natural hair brushes: Powder and eyeshadow brushes are often made with natural hair. These bristles are prone to staining from pigmented products like blush, but discoloration is normal and doesn’t mean the brush isn’t clean. Because natural hair can dry out over time, use a moisturizing soap (like a bar soap you may use on your body) or cleaner to keep the bristles soft and healthy. Once you know what you’re working with, follow these steps: Choose your soap. Liquid dish soap or shampoo both work, but Vosburg prefers bar soap for natural hair brushes because it’s effective, non-drying and easy to use. “When cleaning with a bar of soap, I will simply wet the tips of the brush hairs with a bit of lukewarm water and then swirl the brush a few times on the bar of soap.” There are also plenty of effective cleansers on the market made specifically for makeup brushes.Work the soap into a lather. After swirling the brush on the bar or adding soap to the bristles, move it to the palm of your hand or on a silicone cleaning pad and continue swirling until it lathers. If you’re using liquid soap, a pea-size amount in your palm is enough for any size brush since it’s concentrated, says Hart. Gently wipe the brush back and forth through the soap, taking care not to press or bend the bristles too hard. Rinse. Hold the brush with the bristles pointing down and run only the brush hairs under lukewarm water. Hot water can damage the hair and loosen the glue that holds the bristles in place, says Hart. Try to keep water away from the ferrule, the metal piece that connects the bristles to the handle, since that’s where the glue and binders are. Not dunking or soaking your brushes will help reduce shedding and help them last longer, according to Vosburg.Repeat as needed. Continue lathering and rinsing until the water runs clear and the brush is free of makeup.Remove excess water and dry. Gently squeeze the bristles with a microfiber towel to remove excess water, then lay the brush flat to air dry. articles.title: ‘Wave of freedom’ sweeps Latin America as Trump ally takes fight to Marxist terror group
articles.summary: José Manuel Restrepo says Colombian forces, not American troops, will lead operations against armed groups under Trump's Shield of the Americas.
articles.body: UNITED NATIONS — Colombian Vice President José Manuel Restrepo said his country is embracing President Donald Trump’s push for a new security alliance across the Western Hemisphere, but drew a clear line on the role American forces would play inside Colombia, telling Fox News Digital that Colombian troops — not U.S. forces — will carry out operations against the country’s armed groups. Restrepo spoke with Fox News Digital in an on-camera interview days after joining Trump and other regional leaders at a Shield of the Americas meeting on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York, where Trump called the initiative the "largest and most powerful alliance for economic and national security ever to convene in the Western Hemisphere." Trump urged members to treat what he called "narco terrorists" as common threats and impose sanctions on U.S.-designated terrorist organizations. Restrepo said he personally discussed the region’s changing political and security landscape with Trump. The shift in Colombia comes amid a broader political realignment across Latin America, with De La Espriella’s June victory adding Colombia to a group of countries including Argentina, Chile, Ecuador, Bolivia and Panama that have moved to the right, fueled in part by voter concerns over crime, economic weakness and political instability. TRUMP ALLY 'EL TIGRE' SWORN IN AS COLOMBIA'S NEW PRESIDENT AMID CONTINENT'S RIGHTWARD SHIFT "There is a wave of freedom, a wave of democracy, a wave of free market. … There is a new momentum for the region and we have to take advantage of that momentum. That's what I said to President Trump," Restrepo told Fox News Digital. "If we want to keep and preserve democracy in the region, the Shield of the Americas is going to be the best opportunity to do it." Asked what Trump told him, Restrepo said the president agreed and expressed respect for Colombian President Abelardo De La Espriella. "Colombia is a new partner. In my opinion, it's one of the most important partners for the United States in the region," Restrepo said. That partnership is already being tested in the fight against drug trafficking and armed groups. WHITE HOUSE HIGHLIGHTS 'STEEPEST' EVER DECLINE IN US CASUALTIES FROM CARTELS AMID BOAT STRIKES In August, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said Colombia had authorized "joint military operations to destroy terrorists and terror networks" and told reporters that Washington had discussed possible joint strikes against groups including the National Liberation Army, or ELN, which the U.S. designates as a terrorist organization, and remnants of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia. "Designated terrorist organizations, with partnered governments, will be legitimate targets of the United States government," including in Colombia, Hegseth said when asked whether such operations were expected, according to Reuters. But when pressed by Fox News Digital on whether joint U.S.-Colombian strikes remained an option, Restrepo appeared to narrow the scope of direct American involvement. "The United States helps us on security, helps us information, helps us on technology, but the public forces of Colombia are those who are going to act in those places," he said. US FORCES OBLITERATE SUSPECTED 'NARCO-TERRORIST' VESSEL IN LETHAL EASTERN PACIFIC STRIKE, KILLING 3 Asked specifically whether Colombia would have the "boots on the ground," Restrepo replied: "We will have our group, our public forces on the ground." The tougher posture comes as Colombia confronts renewed violence from armed and drug-trafficking groups. This week, De La Espriella ordered the military into Santa Marta after the Autodefensas Conquistadoras de la Sierra Nevada, an illegal armed group involved in drug trafficking, responded to the killing of one of its senior leaders with an "armed strike," threats, roadblocks and attacks that left businesses shuttered and public transportation disrupted. More than 500 soldiers and 600 police officers were deployed, according to the Colombian presidency. The new government is also seeking to reverse former President Gustavo Petro’s "total peace" policy, which pursued negotiations with several armed organizations. Before taking office, De La Espriella announced that he would dismantle key elements of the policy and reactivate arrest warrants against members of illegal armed groups. Restrepo went further, accusing the former government of creating "the idea of impunity" and saying the new administration instead intends to confront groups it considers terrorists. US, SHIELD OF THE AMERICAS CONDEMN 'ONGOING EFFORTS' TO OVERTHROW BOLIVIA'S ELECTED PRESIDENT AMID UNREST He said that when the new government took office, "around 30%" of Colombia’s regions lacked effective territorial control — a figure Fox News Digital has not independently verified — and said the administration was seeking to regain those areas through stronger security forces, intelligence gathering, drug eradication and extraditions. Restrepo also argued that the same security debate should extend to the United Nations, where Colombia used its General Assembly address this week to call for reforms and an international definition of terrorism. The UN has had a global counterterrorism strategy since 2006, but member states have for decades failed to agree on a comprehensive international convention defining terrorism. Colombia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Thursday also announced that the country was suspending all diplomatic relations with Iran. "This sovereign decision aligns with the pillars guiding the Government's foreign policy regarding national and hemispheric security, as well as the fight against transnational crime, taking into account alleged links between the Iranian government and international terrorist groups and other narcoterrorist groups that threaten the country's security," the Ministry wrote in a statement posted to X. MELANIA TRUMP’S HOME-COUNTRY LEADER RIPS UN ‘DOUBLE STANDARDS’ AS TRUMP PROMISE IS REVEALED "I think this is a moment in which the United Nations have to reflect on its own future," Restrepo told Fox News Digital, calling for greater efficiency and effectiveness as well as international agreement on terrorism. "The only way to attain peace, which is one of the main objectives of the UN, is through confronting terrorism," he said, arguing that countries need greater intelligence sharing, judicial cooperation and coordination. With Secretary-General António Guterres set to leave office at the end of the year, Restrepo said the transition could offer the institution an opportunity to change. "I think that the UN has a new moment and the UN has to take advantage of that opportunity," he said. Restrepo added that the institution also needed to address what he described as the inconsistent application of human rights standards. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Human rights should apply to all, regardless of political considerations," Restrepo said. "Ideology cannot decide to whom we are going to apply or not human rights."

articles.title: 2022 Rajouri IED blast: Police file chargesheet against 4
articles.summary: JAMMU: J&K Police have filed a chargesheet against four terrorists, including a Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba handler, in a 2022 IED blast case.
articles.body: JAMMU: J&K Police have filed a chargesheet against four terrorists, including a Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba handler, in a 2022 IED blast case.Two migrant labourers were injured in the explosion below Jaganaloo bridge in Rajouri district on April 19 that year. Kandi police station subsequently registered an FIR under relevant provisions of the IPC, Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, and Explosive Substances Act.Three of the accused — Talib Hussain Shah, Mohammed Sadiq and Mohammed Shabir, all from Draj in Rajouri’s Kotranka tehsil — are already behind bars. articles.title: Mississippi police seize kratom and make arrests after deaths of Ole Miss students
articles.summary: Two people were arrested and a load of kratom seized, Mississippi authorities said Friday, days following the mysterious deaths of two Ole Miss students who were found with kratom at the scene.
articles.body: Two people were arrested and a load of kratom seized, Mississippi authorities said Friday, days following the mysterious deaths of two Ole Miss students who were found with kratom at the scene. Metro Narcotics agents on Thursday raided the Puffs Vape, Tobacco and Beer Store, located in the 100 block of Heritage Drive in Oxford, officials said. Agents seized “more than 500 units of kratom, along with an assortment of THC cartridges, gummies, and other suspected narcotics,” according to am Oxford police statement,. The possession, distribution and sale of kratom has been prohibited from Oxford in 2019, police said. Yahya Mohamed Mosleh, 51, and Islam Mohamed, 18, were booked for various drug offenses. The store’s owner, 40-year-old Amer Alowdi, was indicted for allegedly trafficking narcotics in 2022, officials said. He fled the country before prosecution and “additional charges may be forthcoming as the investigation continues” in this matter, officials said. Aidan Hamilton, 18, a freshman from Englewood, Colorado, and Robert Strang, 20, a junior from Atlanta, were found dead in separate locations this week, Ole Miss said. Their causes of death have not been announced and it is not clear if kratom played any role. Their deaths sparked renewed concerns about the drug, which officials said was found at the scene of both deaths. Kratom is an herb with opioidlike effects. It has gained popularity in the U.S. as an unapproved treatment for pain, anxiety and drug dependence. Kratom can be stimulating or sedating, depending on the dosage taken, according to the Drug Enforcement Administration. It wasn’t immediately clear on Friday if these arrests have any connection to the Hamilton and Strang deaths. This is a developing story, Please check back here for updates.

articles.title: Flying sports car hides its wings as production gets closer
articles.summary: Samson Sky's Switchblade flying car secures $80 million from Dubai's Matin Group, but the redesigned hybrid-electric aircraft still needs more testing.
articles.body: If you have ever been stuck in traffic wishing your car could sprout wings, Samson Sky has been working on something pretty close. Its Switchblade flying car can drive out of your garage and take you to a nearby airport. Once there, the wings come out, the tail extends and the vehicle becomes an airplane. You heard right, an airplane. After landing, everything folds back inside so you can drive the rest of the way. That idea has been around for years. What makes Switchblade worth another look right now is that Samson says it has secured an $80 million investment from Dubai-based Matin Group. Samson plans to use the funding to help move the project toward U.S. production. The company still needs another $20 million to fully fund its current production plan. That new backing gets the Switchblade closer. But what really caught my attention is how much Samson has changed since we first watched this flying car take off. PILOTLESS CARGO AIRCRAFT COULD CHANGE HOW PACKAGES MOVE NEW! 🩺 Free CyberGuy LIVE class: Get Better Healthcare With AI Saturday, September 26 at 11 a.m. ET / 8 a.m. PT Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson will show you five practical ways AI can help you organize your health history, remember important appointment details, understand complicated medical information, research prescriptions and prepare smarter questions for your doctor. No technical experience is needed. Save your free spot at CyberGuyLive.com. Register and receive the replay and step-by-step guide afterward. This flying sports car makes its wings disappear The latest Switchblade design looks much more like a car when you are using it on the road. Samson says the wings, tail and propeller are now fully enclosed inside the vehicle during driving mode. That is a major change from the earlier design that completed its first flight in November 2023. When you reach an airport, the wings extend and the tail moves into position for flight. Samson says the transformation from driving mode to flying mode takes about three minutes. After you land, the process reverses. The flight hardware folds back inside the body before you continue the trip by road. Samson says that setup allows the Switchblade to fit inside a standard garage while also protecting the flight surfaces when the vehicle is being driven or stored. There is still a runway involved, though. The Switchblade does not take off vertically from your driveway. You drive it to an airport, transform it into flight mode and take off from there. The Switchblade we saw fly in 2023 has changed We first covered the Switchblade after its official first flight on Nov. 5, 2023. The prototype flew from Grant County International Airport in Moses Lake, Washington. Since then, Samson has kept working on the version it hopes to put into customers' hands. The company has changed the design and increased the size of its engine. Samson says it plans to use three production prototypes for more testing around the end of 2026 or beginning of 2027. So while we have already seen a Switchblade get off the ground, the version heading toward production has changed since that 2023 flight. That is why I am especially interested in what happens next. I want to see the latest Switchblade take to the air and show us what this new design can actually do. How fast could the Switchblade flying car go? Samson is targeting some attention-grabbing performance numbers. The company currently lists a maximum airspeed of 190 mph and a maximum flying range of 450 miles. It lists a maximum road speed of 100 mph. Samson also lists a 160 mph cruise speed. However, its FAQ says that anticipated figure still needs verification during production-prototype flight testing. The Switchblade uses a hybrid-electric drivetrain. A gasoline engine powers a generator, which supplies electricity to the vehicle's motors. Samson says the system powers the wheels on the ground and the propellers in flight. The company currently lists a 44-gallon fuel capacity and says the vehicle uses 91-octane automotive gasoline. HELMET-STYLE COCKPIT VISION SYSTEM AIMS TO CHANGE HOW PILOTS SEE IN LOW VISIBILITY $80 million gives the Switchblade production push some muscle Making a flying prototype and building vehicles for customers are two very different challenges. Samson says the new $80 million investment will help establish its first 180,000-square-foot Switchblade production facility in the U.S. The company signed a Joint Investment Agreement with Matin Group, and the two companies have started setting up a joint venture. Where that factory ends up remains an open question. Samson Sky CEO and founder Sam Bousfield tells CyberGuy that the search has narrowed considerably, saying, "We will maintain our Samson Sky R&D Facility in Prineville, OR, and we have narrowed down the US production facility to three potential locations in different parts of the country, with some negotiations already begun." Samson has not identified those locations publicly. There is serious new money behind the production effort, but another financial hurdle remains. Samson says $20 million still needs to be raised before its current production plan is fully funded. When could you actually get one? Samson's current timeline points to summer 2027. The company says it expects its Builder Assist assembly line to be ready by then. Its first year of production will focus mostly on customers who previously paid for some of the earliest delivery positions. Depositors and reservation holders would follow. Then there is the price. Samson currently estimates the Switchblade VFR kit will start at $200,000. The IFR version carries an estimated price of $235,000. Those prices can still change before customer production gets underway. Bousfield tells CyberGuy that reaching this point has been part of the plan for years. "It's been great developing the technology for a flying car that you park in your garage and is high performance in both modes. Now we get to put it out for people to use and explore the world around them." Before that happens, buyers will have to do something you probably have never done when purchasing a car. Yes, you have to help build your Switchblade Buying a Switchblade comes with homework. Samson plans for the aircraft to operate under the Experimental Amateur-Built category in the U.S. FAA rules require the "major portion," meaning more than 50%, of an eligible amateur-built aircraft's fabrication and assembly to be completed by people building it for their own education or recreation. That requirement is often called the 51% rule. Samson says its Builder Assist program will guide owners through their portion of the process. The company says much of its manufacturing process will be automated and computer-driven. It estimates an owner can finish the required work in as little as one week. One regulatory detail deserves some attention here. The FAA says it evaluates aircraft kits to determine whether they can allow a builder to meet the major-portion requirement. The FAA does not approve or certify the kit itself. The finished aircraft also goes through the FAA airworthiness process. So this will be a very different experience from walking into a dealership, signing a few forms and driving home. You will need to know how to fly it too A Switchblade may drive like a vehicle on the ground, but once those wings come out, aviation rules take over. Samson says you will need a private pilot certificate to fly one. Ground licensing can vary based on where you register the vehicle. The company says an automobile or motorcycle license may apply depending on local regulations. That also separates Switchblade from some of the other flying vehicles we have been following. Electric air taxis such as Joby's eVTOL are designed around vertical takeoff and landing. Switchblade takes another route. It uses conventional runways but gives you something an air taxi cannot: the same vehicle stays with you after you land. That could be useful on a regional trip. Instead of landing and then finding a rental car or arranging another ride, you fold the wings away and keep going. WISCONSIN MAN FLIES HELICOPTER TO CABELA'S BECAUSE THE DRIVE WAS TOO LONG What this means to you Here's what makes the Switchblade so interesting to me. You could pull out of your garage, drive to an airport, fly hundreds of miles and then keep driving after you land. No rental car. No waiting around for another ride. The same vehicle goes with you from start to finish. The new funding gets Samson closer to making that happen, but I would not start clearing space in the garage yet. The company still has to finish funding its production plans, choose where to build the Switchblade and put the latest version through more testing. We have seen an earlier prototype fly, but the redesigned vehicle heading toward production still needs to show what it can do in the air. And if you are thinking, "Where do I sign up?" there is a lot more involved than the estimated $200,000 starting price. You will need pilot training and access to an airport. You also have to take part in the Builder Assist process. For me, the next big moment comes when this latest Switchblade leaves the runway. If it can deliver on the speed, range and transformation Samson is targeting, this flying sports car suddenly gets a whole lot more interesting. Kurt's key takeaways What I like about the Switchblade is that the idea makes sense the minute you see how it works. You drive to the airport, fly to another city, fold the wings away after you land and keep going. The latest design makes that even more interesting because all that flight hardware disappears inside a vehicle you can park in your garage. Of course, most of us are not shopping for a $200,000 flying sports car. The price alone puts the Switchblade out of reach for the majority of us, and becoming a pilot adds another wrinkle. But that does not mean you have to be a potential buyer to find this fascinating. I certainly am not planning to put one in my garage tomorrow, but I want to see whether Samson can actually pull this off. The new funding gives Samson a much stronger push toward production, and we have already seen an earlier Switchblade fly. Now I want to see this redesigned version get into the air. If Samson can deliver what it is promising, we could be watching a pretty remarkable idea make the jump from a prototype we have followed for years to a flying sports car people can actually own. Would you trust one vehicle to take you down the highway and into the sky, or would you want to see a few years of customer flights before climbing aboard? articles.title: Police believe Tasia Fortune’s hanging was staged as new details revealed in court
articles.summary: JACKSON, Miss. — Authorities believe Tasia Fortune’s hanging was staged and that she was possibly killed at another location before being found behind an abandoned Mississippi home, a detective said in court Friday.
articles.body: JACKSON, Miss. — Authorities believe Tasia Fortune’s hanging was staged and that she was possibly killed at another location before being found behind an abandoned Mississippi home, a detective said in court Friday. New details about Fortune’s death last month were revealed during a court hearing for Jarques Ratliff, one of the two men arrested and charged with murder. At a court hearing earlier this month, Ratliff, 51, was denied bond after he pleaded not guilty. Fortune, a 29-year-old Black woman, was found hanging from a tree behind the Jackson home on Aug. 3. Officials believe she may have been dead for two or three days before she was found. A motive in the killing and a cause of death have not been released. A detective said at Friday’s hearing that there may have been an issue over missing illegal narcotics. The detective declined to release additional details because the grand jury has not received all of the evidence. Ratliff, 51, told the court that Fortune was his friend. His attorney, Toney Baldwin, said he wants the “truth about what happened to come out.” “My client said he’s not involved and that’s absolutely what I believe,” he said. Fortune’s mother, Christy Spivey, said she wants to know what evidence police have. The other man arrested and charged in Fortune’s death is Earnest Lloyd Jr. Police have also obtained a warrant for a third suspect. Both Lloyd and Ratliff are Black. Lloyd, 25, allegedly had a physical altercation with Fortune either days or minutes before she died, NBC affiliate WLBT of Jackson reported. He was accused of hanging Fortune with a black cable cord, according to the news station. Bracey Harris reported from Jackson, Mississippi, and Minyvonne Burke reported from Pittsburgh.

articles.title: How Israel’s ‘Blue Line’ team seizes Palestinian land in the West Bank
articles.summary: Little-known Israeli map team is redrawing land boundaries as Palestinians face growing illegal settlement expansion.
articles.body:
Al-Mughayyir, occupied West Bank – As the October olive harvest approaches, Bilal Abu Alia stands near his home, gazing at his family’s land – territory he says Israeli authorities have taken from his family in the Palestinian village of al-Mughayyir, northeast of Ramallah.

Of their original 0.4sq km (100 acres) of land, Bilal explains that his family can now only access a small area that includes their home and a few olive trees.

Land confiscation in the occupied West Bank doesn’t always begin with a direct seizure. In many instances, the process starts with the redesignation and demarcation of land on official Israeli maps, with the Israeli Civil Administration’s “Blue Line Team” playing an important role.

According to a report published in mid-September by the National Bureau for Defending Land and Resisting Settlements, a body affiliated with the Palestinian Liberation Organization, the Blue Line team was officially established in 1999. Its primary role is to identify and formally designate areas that Israeli authorities classify as “state land” .

Comprising surveyors, cartographers and legal experts, the team uses modern surveying technology and geographic information systems to review and redraw those boundaries on official maps, according to the bureau.

The significance of the process is that land included within the boundaries Israel recognises as “state land” can subsequently be allocated for settlement projects, which are illegal under international law.

Israel’s Civil Administration has argued that Blue Line revisions are technical corrections of historic surveying errors. But the United Nations has said that the revisions have essentially expanded the boundaries of land classified by Israel as state property.

The bureau report argues that, in recent years, the Blue Line team has evolved from a technical mechanism for boundary demarcation into a tool increasingly used to accelerate settlement expansion and legitimise settlement outposts.

The team recently re-demarcated areas in the northern and central West Bank totalling almost 0.2sq km (49 acres) that were reclassified from “state land” to land designated for settlement activity, according to the office. That included land that belonged to the Palestinian villages of Jalud, Qaryut, Turmusayya and al-Mughayyir.

Al Jazeera has reached out to Israeli authorities for comment, but has yet to receive a response.

In August 2025, an Israeli settler was shot while encroaching on Palestinian land in al-Mughayyir. Israeli forces subsequently launched a four-day operation in the village, during which bulldozers uprooted thousands of olive trees across much of the village, including the land later taken from Bilal’s family.

“We were informed that we were barred from accessing this land, that it had become a military zone and then state land. We watched as the olive trees planted by my great-grandfather a century ago were bulldozed and uprooted right before our eyes, yet we were powerless to stop it,” Bilal told Al Jazeera.

Israel informed the family that the land had become a closed military zone, off-limits to both Palestinians and settlers. However, shortly after, Bilal noticed a settler plowing the land. After the family lodged a complaint with the military liaison office, the settler stopped ploughing for a few days but soon resumed under the protection of the Israeli army.

“Furthermore, in December 2025, months after the olive trees were uprooted, we attempted to gather the debris to at least salvage the wood,” he added. “We discovered that the land was under camera surveillance; my father, my elderly uncle and I were arrested and held for three days handcuffed, blindfolded and left lying on the cold ground at an army camp.”

The land was once a source of livelihood for Bilal’s extended family, but the family says it can no longer farm it. Meanwhile, settlers continue to enter and use land in the area surrounding their home.

The family attempted to file an objection against the confiscation of their land, but Bilal said he was only given three days to file an objection, leaving them no real opportunity to act, while bulldozers had already begun work on the site.

The implications of the Blue Line team’s work go far beyond merely altering colours or boundaries on a map: A reclassification of land to state property can effectively open it up to construction projects or illegal settlement expansion.

In the case of al-Mughayyir, this occurs within the context of broader settlement expansion that, according to the National Bureau, encircles the village and restricts residents’s ability to access and utilise their land.

This mechanism suggests that land seizure often unfolds in stages: The land is first surveyed and boundaries redrawn before being designated ‘state land’ and then designated for settlement expansion.

In the northern West Bank, the measures add to the continued expansion of Israeli settlements around Jenin. For example, the bureau points to military seizure orders affecting land around Qabatiya, near Jenin.

According to the report, Israel has targeted lands belonging to Qabatiya and the surrounding area in recent weeks, with two military orders confiscating a total of almost 14sq km (5.4 sq miles or nearly 3,500 acres).

Raed Moqadi, a researcher at the Land Research Center, told Al Jazeera that the Blue Line team efforts had accelerated in 2026.

“The Palestinian Authority has submitted objections regarding the team’s work to various international institutions and organisations, but these moves haven’t led to a halt in the measures being taken on the ground,” he explained.

The Blue Line team is not the only mechanism affecting control over Palestinian land but instead operates within a wider system involving a web of overlapping measures.

Salah al-Khawaja, a senior official with Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission, told Al Jazeera that the policy of controlling Palestinian land operates within an integrated system comprising settlements, pastoral outposts and settler roads, alongside the separation wall, military zones and training areas.

Al-Khawaja linked the measures to a broader political agenda aimed at entrenching Israeli control over Area C , the area of the West Bank under Israeli military and administrative control, in accordance with a plan published by now Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich in 2017.

Al-Khawaja noted that the legal process is also part of the system. The majority of land-related cases handled by the commission are resolved in favour of settlers and rulings by the Israeli Supreme Court no longer provide adequate protection for Palestinians in land disputes, he said.

For Palestinians whose land is affected, this ultimately means the loss of land that has often been in their family’s hands for generations.

Adnan Kmail, 62, whose family owns land affected by the recent Israeli military orders in al-Mughayyir, told Al Jazeera that he has never received a clear, written notice regarding what he said was the seizure of 0.1 sq km (25 acres) of his property. Instead, he was informed by the local municipality.

He subsequently watched as Israeli bulldozers uprooted olive trees, some over 60 years old, to make way for an army outpost.

The olive trees provided a source of income for Adnan and his extended family – more than 70 people in total. Adnan said the land produced about 5,000kg (1,100 pounds) of olive oil each season, income the families have now lost.

“We didn’t file an objection because we knew it would be futile. We can’t even go near the land; just a few days ago, soldiers shot a man in the leg simply for passing through the area. My heart aches whenever I think of my land,” Adnan said.

articles.body: A small group of Goulburn residents gathered around kitchen tables in late 2014 to discuss a simple idea: making their own clean electricity. Twelve years later, that discussion became Australia’s first community-owned solar farm paired with a large-scale battery. The 1.4-megawatt facility, backed by a four-megawatt-hour battery, officially opened on an old industrial site on the edge of the New South Wales regional city. The project can generate enough electricity to power about 500 homes, sending power directly into the local grid. The project depended on years of shared effort and persistence. About 300 investors, most of them local residents, raised $3.3 million in capital, along with $2.3 million in grants from the NSW Government. According to the Business Council of Co-operatives and Mutuals (BCCM), the project provides a practical example of how regional communities can help lead the move to renewable energy through community ownership.Roots of a decade-long initiativeThe project began with Community Energy for Goulburn (CE4G), a volunteer sub-committee formed by local sustainability group The Goulburn Group. Organisers wanted a system where every member had an equal say, regardless of how much money they invested. They formed the Goulburn Community Energy Cooperative and registered it through the NSW Department of Fair Trading. Under the cooperative structure, each member has one vote. Someone who invested $400 had the same voting power as someone who invested $4,000. This meant no investor could use greater financial power to control the project. Writing in energy publication The Energy, founding member and CE4G president Peter Fraser said building trust began with the local community. Before making formal applications, volunteers went door to door around the proposed solar farm to explain the idea and hear people's concerns. Fraser wrote that there were no objections from those neighbours. The chosen site was an old, unused industrial site beside the railway corridor between Sydney and Canberra. The land was not square and was not ideally aligned to face north, which created some design challenges. But the site was easy to see from the road and railway, giving the project a public showcase. It was also next to an existing 33kV power line, which made the grid connection easier.Navigating delays and unexpected hurdlesDelays, policy changes and rising costs repeatedly pushed the project timeline out. Organisers dealt with global supply problems during the pandemic, higher material costs and long reviews by the local council and electricity network owner. Because the solar farm is inside the Sydney water catchment area, the project also faced extra planning rules. Fraser wrote in The Energy that Sydney Water required considerable landscaping measures to help stop sediment from reaching catchment dams. These requirements added more work before construction could begin. Tax rules also surprised the organisers. As Fraser explained in The Energy, government grants for capital projects can be taxable, so tax had to be paid before the solar farm was earning any income. Fraser wrote that the project team had not known about this, and that the government that provided the original grant had not known either. The work continued with specialist project developer Komo Energy, which stayed involved for more than eight years. Fraser credited the company with helping the cooperative through the many challenges involved in developing the project.Keeping financial benefits within the townUnlike commercial power projects owned by outside shareholders, the cooperative model keeps much of the financial benefit in the local economy. Local contractors and suppliers were used for construction and ongoing work where possible. At the official opening, Parliamentary Secretary to the NSW Treasurer David Mehan MP praised the cooperative's local economic impact. “The co-operative model has grounded this project in the region,” Mehan said. “It has anchored it ethically and in the way it has been delivered, from using local businesses to keeping benefits local. Around 80 per cent of profit remains in this community. Few renewable energy projects in NSW can say that. The co-operative model has made it possible here in Goulburn.” BCCM Chief Executive Melina Morrison also praised the long effort made by the local volunteers. “You started with an idea and now you own an energy asset,” Morrison told members. “You have walked together, showing together we are stronger.”A working template for regional energyCommunity Energy for Goulburn plans to remain an incorporated association and explore more renewable energy projects in the region. The separate cooperative board, elected by members, oversees the commercial operation of the solar farm and its battery. The four-megawatt-hour battery stores extra electricity produced during the day and can send that power into the grid later, when demand is higher. This allows the project to avoid relying as heavily on lower midday wholesale electricity prices. Peter Fraser explained in The Energy that the battery lets the project sell more power at times when prices are higher, usually in the afternoon. The project shows that a small regional community can raise money, build and manage complex grid infrastructure when it has enough time, commitment and a clear structure for ownership. For Goulburn, twelve years of volunteer meetings and community work have ended with a working clean-energy asset that sends electricity into the local grid.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 1994, Yellowstone began removing invasive lake trout; by 2024 crews had taken out over 4.9 million as native cutthroat trout showed signs of recovery
articles.summary: Yellowstone Lake and the Yellowstone River support the largest remaining inland population of Yellowstone cutthroat trout.
articles.body: Yellowstone Lake and the Yellowstone River support the largest remaining inland population of Yellowstone cutthroat trout. The National Park Service has been protecting this population from the predatory threat for three decades now. Gillnetting to suppress non‑native lake trout began in 1994, the same year they were first discovered in Yellowstone Lake, with early removal efforts expanded in 2001. Based on the data provided by Yellowstone Forever, the official fundraising partner for the park, it was noted that over 4.9 million lake trout have been harvested from Yellowstone Lake up until 2024, with 264,650 in 2024 only. This article outlines the history of the invasion, its progression and outcomes, and presents findings from a recent 2024 study that identify additional obstacles in the process.Lake trout were stocked elsewhere in the park in 1890 and first detected in Yellowstone Lake in 1994As per the records of the U.S. Fish Commission, lake trout were intentionally introduced in Lewis and Shoshone lakes in 1890. At that time, the lakes had no fish. In the following 100 years, lake trout became established in Yellowstone Lake, where the fish were initially found in 1994. Following verification that lake trout were breeding, an expert group was convened by the park. It was determined that suppression measures were required to conserve the native cutthroat trout, but that this would be a never-ending task. Direct removal methods, like gill netting, were recommended. According to the article, part of the problem may be the lake's deep water. Lake trout inhabit deep waters in which few predators can venture, so eagles, osprey, pelicans, otters, and grizzly bears have no alternative but the cutthroat trout.Gillnetting has been used since 1995 and expanded more than 10-fold in 2001 with a Great Lakes-style boatAccording to a Yellowstone Science article on the suppression program, early removal efforts were expanded in 2001. The lake added a gillnetting boat of the Great Lakes variety, numerous nets, and staff members to net all summer. As noted by the U.S. Geological Survey, the suppression measures on Yellowstone Lake have led to a tenfold increase in gillnetting since 2010, resulting in a doubling of lake trout caught yearly.However, increasing catches with increasing efforts indicated that the fish population continued to increase. Managers requested an intensive investigation and set the objective of restoring the lake trout population to its mid-1990s level. Modeling done by fisheries scientists showed that there was an abundance of lake trout in Yellowstone Lake during 2012.More than 4.9 million were removed by the end of 2024, including 264,650 that yearHowever, it has gone down from its height. According to Yellowstone Forever, crews harvested 396,950 lake trout from Yellowstone Lake in 2017 as part of the Native Fish Conservation Program. Yellowstone National Park itself has estimated the figure at 282,892 in 2019 and 236,853 in 2023, with the total caught over 30 years of netting efforts (1994 to 2023) exceeding 4.5 million. The National Park Service's fish-management website lists a total of more than 5.1 million lake trout removed since 1994, while Yellowstone Forever's estimate, including 2024, is lower at more than 4.9 million. The scale of the fishing effort is immense. According to the 2022 Native Fish Conservation Program Report of Yellowstone National Park, suppression crews deployed 89,320 gillnet units (net‑nights) to target invasive lake trout. Forty miles of net were fished in the lake daily, and more than 5,500 miles of net were used over the season.Mature lake trout down 80% to 90%, and cutthroat signs improving but below targetsThe netting has taken its toll on the important fish species. Park modeling from 2019 to 2021 showed that the abundance of lake trout aged six years and older had declined by more than 80% from the 2012 peak. Yellowstone Forever estimates that mature lake trout have been reduced by up to 90%. The Yellowstone Science report on recovery monitoring shows that cutthroat trout numbers had not fully recovered even before the latest gains. In 2016, anglers recorded a catch rate of 0.9 cutthroat per hour, the third highest in 11 years but below the park's target of 1.5 to 2.0 per hour. Cutthroat indicators have since trended positively. According to Yellowstone Forever in 2019, spawning fish increased in tributaries, the lake held three times as many young fish, and catch rates rose. Even so, the recovery has not been fully achieved.A 2024 Fisheries study by Glassic and colleagues ties cutthroat recovery to disease and lake levelsA 2024 study in Fisheries, led by U.S. Geological Survey fish biologist Hayley Glassic, built a food web model of Yellowstone Lake that tracks five age classes each of lake trout and cutthroat. According to the study, modeling of Yellowstone Lake for the period 2020-2050 through an Ecopath approach using historical data indicates that it is possible to meet the recovery benchmarks for cutthroat trout, but this would happen only if certain specific conditions prevail. In addition, lake trout diets are found to vary depending on their density; amphipods become predominant while cutthroat trout become less dominant. The study also examined whirling disease, a parasitic illness that infects young trout. Certain spawning streams like Pelican Creek and the Yellowstone River downstream of the lake outlet had 100 percent prevalence of infection. The prevalence of whirling disease in the cutthroat trout population within the lake was between 10 percent and 20 percent.Why netting continues, according to the National Park ServiceAccording to the authorities, it is still impossible to kill lake trout at present due to existing technologies. They reproduce fast enough to prevent their number from decreasing without active elimination. Gillnets were deployed, and experiments are being conducted on killing eggs using plant-based pellets on spawning beds. It seems that it is a good solution for further maintenance of the population after achieving desired results. Fishing people must kill all the lake trout they catch in such zones where they pose a danger to native species. But anglers' contribution is quite small since anglers killed only 3% of all the fish in 2016.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
